critical_code_review_comments: motion.jsx Words: whileInView triggers when the h1 is already inside the initial viewport (hero above the fold), so the initial={{opacity:0,y:18}} state is effectively skipped on the very first paint on tall viewports. Users on short viewports (< ~600px) will see the intended word-by-word cascade; on 4000px viewport tests all 9 opacities read 1 immediately. Not a bug per spec but worth noting: consider replacing whileInView with animate for the hero headline so the cascade is guaranteed regardless of initial scroll position.

Landing.jsx line 89-90 renders TWO <Words as='h1'> blocks side-by-side (`hero-headline` has 9 words, then a second h1 'every client app.' with delay 0.55). The second h1 has no data-testid, which is fine for the spec, but the DOM has two <h1> tags in the same header — accessibility-wise consider making the second one a <span> or visually one heading.

Dashboard.jsx CountUp target for stat-tenants uses the raw app count without filtering by status, so 'Tenants' can differ from the visible/filtered card list once kind-filter is applied. Confirmed: after clicking kind-filter-app-btn, stat card still reads 8 while only 5 cards render. Consider re-computing stats from the filtered set OR labeling clearly (currently label 'TENANTS' is the global total, which is arguably correct).

studio.py _ensure_ids line 131 uses setdefault on style.effects which means an existing block with style.effects={} (empty dict) will NOT get reveal/hover backfilled. All 6 currently-seeded apps happen to have non-empty effects so tests pass, but a legacy imported site with style.effects={} would render without motion. Consider: if not b['style'].get('effects'): b['style']['effects'] = {...}.
